response.description:
Azure Container Linux is a container-optimized, immutable operating system for
AKS node pools — derived from Flatcar Container Linux and built on Azure Linux
RPM packages. It delivers a locked-down, minimal host purpose-built for running
containerized workloads at scale. Key features include: Immutable by design — The root /usr directory is
read-only with dm-verity integrity verification. There is no package manager on
the host — what ships in the image is what runs in production. This eliminates
configuration drift and ensures consistent node state across your fleet. Container-optimized — Minimal OS footprint with
only the components needed to run Kubernetes workloads. Out-of-the-box security — SELinux in enforcing mode applies strict least-privilege policies to all processes. Trusted Launch with a Unified Kernel Image (UKI) verifies boot integrity from firmware through kernel, ensuring nodes haven't been tampered with before they join your cluster. Derived from Flatcar — Built on Flatcar Container Linux's proven architecture: declarative node configuration, systemd-first service management, and an operational model designed for fleets of immutable nodes. Built on Azure Linux — Powered by the Azure Linux RPM ecosystem with Microsoft's security patching cadence, CVE response SLAs, and integrated support through Azure. Learn more and get started:  Tech Community blog post Azure Container Linux Documentation Azure Linux Documentation Azure Linux on GitHub
response.title: Azure Container Linux (ACL) now generally available on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
